listing.name: Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance (OpenXWA)
listing.summary: A native engine for X-Wing Alliance using your own original game data.

steps.title: Choose your original game data
steps.instruction: Select your complete installed X-Wing Alliance folder. For a raw CD copy, use the upstream instructions to merge the contents of ALLIANCE into the game root first.

steps.title: Start the Linux player
steps.instruction: Choose the official v0.0.17 linux-x86_64-release.tar.xz. Extract it into a folder you manage. Portcove Download can unpack it into a new setup folder. Keep the resources, shaders and lib folder beside OpenXWA. Run OpenXWA with glibc 2.35 or later, the GCC 12 runtime or newer, and a Vulkan driver.

warnings: Back up the entire effective profile, all original game folders, and the working player before updating. If the profile cannot be opened, check the working directory for pilots, settings and other files.

references.title: Open the Apple silicon Mac app
references.instruction: Mount the upstream v0.0.17 macos-arm64-release.dmg and copy OpenXWA.app out of it. Use Apple silicon, macOS 13 or later and Metal. Keep the app bundle intact and maintain this copy outside Portcove.

references.title: Keep your settings and pilots
references.instruction: The normal SDL profile is TotallyOpen/OpenXWA under the Linux data home or Mac Application Support. Keep the whole profile with the player closed.

presentation.manual_preparation: On Play, keep the normal in-process setup picker and select your own complete X-Wing Alliance GOG/Steam installation. Preserve the complete original data and package resources, shaders and DLLs. Native 64-bit engine replacement is separate from original-game patch/mod preparation. Multiplayer is not implemented by the selected upstream; no network or mod compatibility is promised. Normal user settings, pilots, replays and temporary files belong to the current account’s SDL preference directory TotallyOpen/OpenXWA; preserve that WHOLE effective profile and every original-data root. Config defaults inside resources are immutable package files, separate from user config.yaml. Core manages only the engine and the listed local config files, not shared external profiles. If SDL profile lookup fails, user/temporary output can fall back to the executable working directory. Arbitrarily named pilots, replays and cache/temp files there are unclaimed modified-runtime data: existing guards refuse destructive maintenance while retaining the creating runtime. A Core backup of declared files does not back up those unknown files. Preserve the WHOLE creating runtime and all effective profiles before reviewing recovery; do not delete files to force an update or assume re-download repairs saves. No automatic migration, portable-pilot backup, backward-save conversion or automatic recovery is offered.
